bio.statement: Vivian says he used the G.I. Bill to earn his education and understands challenges facing veterans, young students and small farmers.
bio.excerpt: As a U.S. Navy veteran who used the G.I. Bill to earn my education, I understand the challenges facing our veterans, young students, and small farmers.

positions.statement: Vivian says he opposes IP28, which he says would criminalize farming, hunting and ranching practices.
positions.excerpt: I strongly oppose IP28. This extreme measure would criminalize everyday farming, hunting, and ranching practices that Oregon families have relied on for generations.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet, General Election Nov. 3, 2026 (Book 4, p. 42)

positions.statement: Vivian describes himself as the only pro-life candidate in the race.
positions.excerpt: I am the only pro-life candidate in this race, and I believe every child deserves a chance at life.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet, General Election Nov. 3, 2026 (Book 4, p. 42)

positions.statement: Vivian says he homeschooled his children because he believes parents, not unions, know what is best for their children.
positions.excerpt: I also chose to homeschool our kids because parents, not unions, know what’s best for their children.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet, General Election Nov. 3, 2026 (Book 4, p. 42)

positions.statement: Vivian's statement asks why more taxes, why poor school scores and why high state salaries.
positions.excerpt: Trust but verify is my motto— why more taxes; why poor school scores; why high state salaries?

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet, General Election Nov. 3, 2026 (Book 4, p. 42)

positions.statement: Vivian says higher education must deliver results such as skills for well-paying jobs in growing fields.
positions.excerpt: I know higher education must deliver real results: training skills that lead to good-paying jobs in growing fields.
